description: Ambiguous intent — vague phrasing, implicit requirements, multi-step reasoning

cases.natural_language: How are we doing this quarter?
cases.expected_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE order_date >= DATE_TRUNC('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) ORDER BY month
cases.description: Vague question requiring inference of 'doing' = revenue/orders and 'this quarter' = current

cases.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1
cases.description: 'Best' is ambiguous — could mean by revenue, quantity, or rating

cases.natural_language: Which customers haven't ordered anything in the last 6 months but were active before that?
cases.expected_sql: SELECT c.name, MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING MAX(o.order_date) < CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months' AND MAX(o.order_date) >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '12 months'
cases.description: Requires reasoning about two time windows: inactive recently but active before

cases.natural_language: Are sales trending up or down?
cases.expected_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '12 months' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)) SELECT month, revenue, revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS change, CASE WHEN revenue > LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) THEN 'Up' WHEN revenue < LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) THEN 'Down' ELSE 'Flat' END AS trend FROM monthly ORDER BY month
cases.description: Requires inferring time window, computing deltas, and labeling direction

cases.natural_language: Find customers who consistently order every month — show their streak
cases.expected_sql: WITH monthly_orders AS (SELECT customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)), with_gaps AS (SELECT customer_id, month, month - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month) * INTERVAL '1 month') AS grp FROM monthly_orders), streaks AS (SELECT customer_id, MIN(month) AS streak_start, MAX(month) AS streak_end, COUNT(*) AS streak_months FROM with_gaps GROUP BY customer_id, grp) SELECT c.name, s.streak_start, s.streak_end, s.streak_months FROM streaks s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id WHERE s.streak_months >= 3 ORDER BY s.streak_months DESC
cases.description: Gap-and-island problem requiring advanced SQL reasoning
